quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Lock the ignition and remove the key.
Set the parking brake.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.
Busy sidewalk.

questions.explanation: This sign warns of a pedestrian crossing. Watch for people crossing the street. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. You should:

options.text: Not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Hide from your friend that you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes before driving to learn how the vehicle works and where all controls are located.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes before driving to learn how the vehicle works and where all controls are located.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take time to learn where the turn signals, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn are located and how they work. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: You may cross double solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Under no conditions.

questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into a driveway or to turn onto or off a highway.

questions.question: The best way to deal with tailgaters is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.
Slam on your brakes to get the other driver to back off.
Change lanes or slowly down to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slowly down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to notice if someone is tailgating you. If they are, slow down gradually and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen when a vehicle follows too closely.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Before stopping, check your mirrors and blind spots.
Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before braking.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. When stopping, release the gas first to let your vehicle slow down. Then press the brake pedal smoothly to stop.

questions.question: To reduce the effects of headlight glare at night, you should look:

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, look at the right side of the road. Do not look directly at the bright headlights or you may be blinded for several seconds.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use turn signals when changing lanes, parking, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area. Signals tell other drivers what you are doing and help prevent accidents.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign:

options.text: Try to drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are coming and keep driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing signs warn you that a train may be nearby. Obey all railroad crossing signs and barriers. Never go around lowered gates.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are merely suggestions.
Must be followed only when other cars are present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly that they may look drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they may look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they may look drunk. Opening a window, turning on the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert to road hazards.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and turn carefully back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and turn carefully back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without braking hard. Then turn carefully back onto the pavement. Watch for other traffic when you return to the road.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol?

options.text: They are always aware of the risks they are taking.
They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
They are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.
They have faster reaction times.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol hurts judgment, vision, concentration, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Steep downgrade.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you about a steep hill ahead. You should slow down to avoid brake damage or a crash.

questions.question: What shape and color is a slow-moving vehicle emblem?

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles using this emblem drive 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: To turn left on a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.explanation: To turn left on multilane streets and highways, start from the left lane.

questions.question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp, what should a driver do?

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Has the right-of-way.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When you enter an interstate from an entrance ramp, you must yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge into traffic safely when you can.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Call the police immediately.
Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Flash your lights to show the aggressive driver they are wrong.
Drive aggressively back at the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to get back at them can make the situation worse and more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Side road.
Two-way left turn.
Farm machinery.

questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs tell drivers to stop and give the right-of-way to other traffic. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.
When turning left or right.
When changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. Look over your shoulder when you turn, change lanes, or pull toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Lines that divide traffic moving in opposite directions are ____.

options.text: White
Red
Black
Yellow

questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are coming to the intersection.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop, let other traffic go, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Traffic signals use arrows to control turns from certain lanes. What does a green arrow mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
It means go, and you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
It means go only if a circular green light is also showing.
It points toward an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means go, and you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. You must turn in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep hill ahead.
People crossing ahead.
Low railroad crossing.
Low clearance.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that the bridge or overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: When can you pass another car on the shoulder?

options.text: When the car ahead is turning.
When the car ahead is going too slowly.
When you don't see any pedestrians.
Never.

questions.explanation: You must never drive off the road or onto the shoulder to pass another car.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A volunteer group is cleaning the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
A pedestrian crosswalk is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or near the road ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After the turn, your car should be in:

options.text: The right lane.
The center of the street.
The left lane.
The lane with the least traffic.

questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, finish your turn in the lane closest to the lane you just left.

questions.question: Which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way when turning left?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.explanation: A green arrow lets you proceed in the direction it points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: Do not pass when:

options.text: You see a hill or curve.
A school bus has flashing lights.
You are near an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Never pass on a hill, on a curve, at an intersection, on a railroad crossing, on a bridge, or in any no passing zone. Do not pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: When stopped by police or at a vehicle check, what must you show?

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Your driver's license.
Proof of registration.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must carry and show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance when driving.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain has stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the road surface. Hot weather makes this worse because heat and water together push more oil to the surface.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift the car to neutral and press the brake pedal with steady pressure. When it is safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: You are in the right lane on an expressway. When should you move to the left lane?

options.text: When traffic is heavy but moving steadily.
When the weather is bad and roads are slippery.
When traffic is slow in your lane and cars are in the left lane.
When traffic is light and cars are merging onto the expressway from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic is light and cars are merging onto the expressway from the right.
questions.explanation: Watch for cars entering the expressway. Move to another lane or adjust your speed to let merging cars enter safely.

questions.question: When a flagger directs traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal traffic laws instead of the flagger's directions.

questions.explanation: Always follow directions from flaggers, signs, or police in construction zones. Not following them is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: How does the type of alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer has less effect than wine.
Wine has less effect than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks have the most effect.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol can harm your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream matters.

questions.question: What kind of blind spots do larger vehicles have?

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: The bigger a vehicle is, the bigger its blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that cannot be seen in the side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Driving aggressively.
Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
More dangerous than not driving defensively.
A bad idea.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe strategies to prevent crashes. You adjust your driving for weather, how you feel, and what other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians are doing.

questions.question: What is a common cause of crashes?

options.text: Drivers going too fast for conditions.
Drivers checking their mirrors and blind spots often.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers keeping a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always drive at or below the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting cars in your blind spot?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Check that your blind spot is clear. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing in front of your car. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful around children. Always give pedestrians in crosswalks the right-of-way.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers did not see motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians even when looking. These are harder to spot because they are smaller, move faster, and have less visible lights. Always watch for these smaller road users to prevent crashes.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Let pedestrians and vehicles cross safely, even if you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say no to a drink by saying you are driving.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.explanation: The best way to avoid crashes from drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe choices after you start drinking.

questions.question: What driving technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Leave the highway as quickly as possible.
Use four-wheel drive.
Slow down and stay farther from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snow or ice. This and increasing your distance from other vehicles are the most important ways to avoid crashes in bad weather.

questions.question: If you see this sign, you:

options.text: Must not pass another vehicle.
May pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
May pass if you know the road.
May pass at night only.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white, rectangular signs with black markings. Drivers must follow all rules on regulatory signs. Where this sign is posted, passing other vehicles is not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
Flagger ahead.
Two-way left turn.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic speed and movement. This sign tells drivers that left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic at a school, you must:

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the guard says something different.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal rules as if no children are present.

questions.explanation: Slow down and follow directions from signs, crossing guards, or police officers. Always drive slowly and carefully in school zones.

questions.question: What should you adjust first when you get in a car to drive?

options.text: Your seat belt.
The steering wheel.
Your rearview mirror.
Your seat.

questions.explanation: First, adjust your seat so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel based on your seat position.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on your phone.
Changing the radio or CD.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions for every mile driven. You must focus fully on driving. Any other task can be dangerous.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should you stop?

options.text: You do not have to stop.
Just slow down to see if crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet on both sides, even if you enter the intersecting roadway.
Stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Without a stop line or crosswalk, stop at the closest point to the intersection where you can see traffic clearly. Do not enter the intersection just to get a better view.
